To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CPF subunits Rna14, Rna15, Cet1, and Cft2, as well as Glc7, are required for the dephosphoryla-tion of the RNA polymerase II (Pol II) C-terminal domain (Pol II CTD) at the 3′-end of protein-coding transcripts.
the CTD tyrosines are a substrate for CPF and that Glc7 is responsible for the phosphatase activity of CPF.

the cleavage-and-polynucleotide-polymerase-factor (CPF) subunit Glc 7 dephosphorates tyrosine residues of the CTD of RNA polymerase (pol) II and that this is essential for termination of transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate transcription termination in eukaryotes.
the molecular mechanisms that control transcription termination in eukaryotes.
the molecular mechanisms of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription termination and how it is coordinated with pre-mRNA processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CPF subunit GlC7 dephosphorates the Pol II CTD at the 3′ end of genes, and that this is required for transcription termination.
the Glc7 phosphatase is required for termination, and the Glc7-dependent dephosphorylating activity of the CPF is involved.
the Glc7-dependent CTD Tyr1 dephoshorylation is required for the efficient termination of Pol II transcription in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Glc7 is the key enzyme that coordinates pre-mRNA processing with Pol II termination in yeast.
Glc7-dependent dephosphoryation of Pol II CTD at the polyA site is required for the recruitment of the termination factors Pcf-11 and Rtt-103 and thus the completion of transcription.
CPF subunit Gl7 is required for transcription termination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CPF subunits Glc7 and Ccr4, in addition to their well-known role in mRNA degradation, also play a role in transcription termination.
the cleavage-and-ployadenylation factor (CPA) of the yeast Saccharomyces cervisiae is an RNA polymerase II CTD phosphatase and this activity is required for transcription termination.
Glc7 is an important player in Pol II transcription termination and that it does so by dephosphorylating Pol II Tyr1.
